claims.claim: Getting a new passport after marriage is not legally required.
claims.quote: You do not need to get a new passport if you: change your address or contact details get a new job change your appearance slightly - for example, dye your hair or grow a beard change your marital status (divorce, marry or form a civil partnership) but keep your name
claims.note: The text says no new passport is needed when marrying without changing name, but does not state a general legal rule after marriage.

claims.claim: Getting a passport in a new name after marriage is strongly recommended.
claims.quote: You’ll need to get a new passport to travel abroad or prove your identity if you change any of the following: your name
claims.note: The text says a new passport is needed for travel or identity proof after a name change, without calling it a strong recommendation.

claims.claim: Use a marriage certificate for a passport in the new name.
claims.quote: Send your marriage or civil partnership certificate when you apply for a passport in your new name - this includes double-barrelled names.
claims.note: The page explicitly requires the certificate for a new-name passport after marriage.

claims.claim: A marriage certificate is supporting evidence for the passport name change.
claims.quote: Send your marriage or civil partnership certificate when you apply for a passport in your new name - this includes double-barrelled names.
claims.note: The page explicitly names the marriage certificate.

claims.claim: A deed poll is supporting evidence for the passport name change.
claims.quote: You can change your name on your passport with one of the following documents: a deed poll a statutory declaration an affidavit
claims.note: The page explicitly names a deed poll for a passport name change.
